en: The Second Book of Pairs (Dukanipāta), Chapter on the Bīraṇa Thicket (Bīraṇathambhavagga)
8. The Kūṭavāṇija Jātaka “This is the cunning of the crafty, well-considered;
this is the counter-cunning of the deceiver against the deceiver.”
If mice were to eat the ploughshare,
why would hawks not carry off the boy?
For there are indeed crooks among the crooks.
And it happens that the deceitful person suffers through his own deceit:
"Give a ploughshare to one who has lost his son and needs a ploughshare;
do not let your own son become one who needs a ploughshare."
The Eighth Jātaka: The Story of the Cheating Merchant.
